name: Sinus Tachycardia
summary: Physiologic response to fever, hypovolemia, pain, hypoxia, sepsis. Treat the underlying cause; do NOT give beta-blockers for compensatory tachycardia.

name: Atrial Fibrillation (AFib)
summary: Absent distinct P-waves, chaotic baseline. If unstable: synchronized cardioversion (120-200 J). If stable: rate control (IV Diltiazem or Metoprolol), stroke risk reduction (anticoagulation).

name: Atrial Flutter
summary: Sawtooth 'F' flutter waves prominent in II, III, aVF. Rate control, anticoagulation, synchronized cardioversion if unstable, catheter ablation long-term.

name: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT)
summary: Re-entrant SVT. If unstable: synchronized cardioversion. If stable: vagal maneuvers, then rapid IV push Adenosine (6 mg followed by 12 mg with saline flush).

name: Ventricular Tachycardia (VT)
summary: Monomorphic or polymorphic. Pulseless: CPR + immediate unsynchronized defibrillation. Unstable with pulse: synchronized cardioversion (100 J). Stable: IV Amiodarone 150 mg over 10 min.

name: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF)
summary: Cardiac arrest. Immediate CPR + Defibrillation (120-200 J biphasic), IV Epinephrine 1 mg q3-5min, IV Amiodarone 300 mg (1st dose) / 150 mg (2nd dose).

name: Symptomatic Sinus Bradycardia
summary: If symptomatic (hypotensive, dizzy, diaphoresis): IV Atropine 1 mg rapid push (repeat q3-5m to max 3 mg), prepare transcutaneous pacing, Epinephrine or Dopamine infusion.

name: 2nd Degree AV Block Mobitz II
summary: Fixed PR interval with sudden dropped QRS complexes. High risk of immediate progression to Complete Heart Block. Attach pacing pads immediately; prepare temporary/permanent pacing.

name: 3rd Degree (Complete) Heart Block
summary: P-waves and QRS complexes completely independent. Atropine usually ineffective. Immediate transcutaneous pacing, prepare transvenous pacing, urgent cardiology/ICU.

name: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
summary: J-point ST elevation >= 1 mm in limb leads or >= 1.5 - 2.5 mm in precordial leads in contiguous leads. Urgent cath lab activation (<90 min door-to-balloon), chewable Aspirin 325 mg, Heparin, dual antiplatelets.

name: Hyperkalemia (Peaked T-Waves)
summary: Tall, peaked, tented T-waves, widening QRS heralds sine-wave arrest. 3-step stabilization: (1) IV Calcium Gluconate (membrane stabilization), (2) IV Insulin + D50 + inhaled Albuterol (intracellular shift), (3) Lokelma / Furosemide / Dialysis (excretion).

name: Hypokalemia & Hypomagnesemia
summary: ST depression, flattened/inverted T-waves, prominent U-waves in V2-V3. High ectopy & Torsades risk. Replenish Potassium Chloride (target > 4.0 mEq/L) and IV Magnesium Sulfate.

name: Critical QTc Prolongation (> 500 ms)
summary: QTc > 500 ms poses severe danger of polymorphic VT (Torsades de Pointes). Discontinue all QT-prolonging drugs immediately (Zofran, Amiodarone, Haloperidol), check lytes, give IV Magnesium Sulfate (2 g over 1-2 min).

name: Left Bundle Branch Block (LBBB)
summary: Broad notched R-wave in I, aVL, V5-V6; deep QS complex in V1. New LBBB with ischemic symptoms is considered STEMI-equivalent (apply Sgarbossa criteria).
